label: <DEL> step of length-3 sequences starting with k/l/d/y/r
explanation: Fires only on the delimiter step (100% of mass), and only in very short sequences: L=3 holds 88% of the mass (2% of L=3 delimiters fire), L=4 the other 12%, and it never fires for L>=5 or at any original-input or copy step. Within those steps it depends on token identity, mostly the first original token, which is the one about to be output: k (46% of mass, and every top example), then l, d, y, r. The last input token also matters (j, 1, i, 3, u are enriched). Magnitude is highest for L=3 with first token k. The predicate gets most of the mass, but precision is only about 0.5: many L=3 delimiters starting with these tokens stay silent, often when the last token is r, k, l, q, w or z. Adding a last-token filter did not raise F1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: k, l, d, y, r, w; least: g, j, -, p) and the third original token (most: 1, j, i, 3, u, y; least: o, n, r, w); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=3, L=3, t=3.
